name: Bottom app bar
statusNote: The fixed bottom app bar is unchanged from M3. The flexible variant (configurable height/spacing, no FAB cradle) is new in Expressive and shares metrics with the docked-toolbar tokens.
summary: A bar anchored to the bottom of the screen carrying a handful of frequent actions and, optionally, an embedded FAB. Use the fixed variant for a stable 80dp bar; use the flexible variant when the bar's height or item spacing needs to adapt to its content. MDC-Android recommends the docked toolbar instead for new designs.

inputs.name: content
inputs.description: The row's action items (icon or text buttons) and, for the fixed variant, an optional floating action button.

inputs.name: flexible
inputs.description: Selects the flexible variant (configurable height/spacing, no FAB cradle) instead of the fixed 80dp bar.

inputs.name: horizontalArrangement
inputs.description: How content is arranged along the row. "start" is the fixed variant's only arrangement; "space-between" and "fixed-centered" apply to the flexible variant.

inputs.name: expandedHeight
inputs.description: Flexible variant only: the maximum height the bar can reach when fully expanded, in dp. Must be finite and greater than zero or the token default is used.

inputs.name: scrollBehavior
inputs.description: exit-always is the only scroll behaviour offered for either variant; it hides the bar 1:1 with scroll.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: Full-width surface, no corner rounding, in both variants.

anatomy.name: Action items
anatomy.description: A row of icon/text buttons: Arrangement.Start (fixed) or a configurable arrangement (flexible).

anatomy.name: Floating action button
anatomy.description: Fixed variant only: an optional dedicated slot at the row's trailing edge.

anatomy.name: Primary action
anatomy.description: Flexible variant: no dedicated FAB slot; a FAB or any other control is just another row child, positioned by the arrangement.

variants.description: Stable 80dp bar, actions start-aligned, FAB embedded top-end.
Shorter bar, actions pushed to the two ends; the flexible variant's default arrangement.
Same flexible bar, items evenly spaced and centered instead.

layout.text: Fixed bar content padding is sized to compensate for the icon button's own touch-target expansion so the visual icon sits 16dp from the edge.

When a FAB is supplied it sits in a top-start-aligned box, again sized so the FAB's own hit-target inset nets out to a clean margin. There is no cradle/notch cut into the container, unlike the legacy MDC-Android MaterialToolbar-based bar — the FAB simply overlaps the top of the bar.

The flexible bar reuses the same container (colour, shape, draggable/scroll plumbing) but swaps in docked-toolbar metrics: height defaults to container-height, content padding uses container-leading-space/container-trailing-space on the horizontal edges only — there is no vertical content padding, since the row is vertically centered in the fixed container height.

Two horizontal arrangements are provided for the flexible bar: the default is space-between, pushing content to the two ends; the alternate fixed-centered arrangement centers items with a maximum spacing between them for a compact, grouped look.

Both variants compute their live height the same way: on layout, the container's measured height becomes the scroll behaviour's heightOffsetLimit (the bar can collapse its own full height, not a fraction of it), and the displayed height is (measuredHeight + heightOffset) coerced to at least 0 — so a fully hidden bar has an on-screen height of exactly 0.

states.label: scroll-hidden
states.text: The bar tracks scroll 1:1 with no threshold — heightOffset is adjusted by the full scroll delta on every post-scroll event, so it starts hiding on the very first pixel of downward scroll and starts reappearing on the very first pixel scrolled back up.

behaviour.text: Action items are standard icon/text buttons; see that component's spec for interaction states.
The bar is directly draggable when an unpinned scroll behaviour is attached, using the same drag-to-resize mechanism as the top app bar.
Scroll behaviour is disabled under touch exploration and the bar stays fully shown.

The fixed bar's default embedded-FAB colour is the secondary FAB container, not the primary container. The flexible bar has no equivalent default-colour hook: since the FAB is just row content, its colour is whatever the caller composes.

Fling/snap uses the same decay-then-snap mechanism as the top app bar, but snapping to fully open (collapsedFraction < 0.5) or fully closed (>= 0.5) uses a faster spring than the top bar's default-effects; the fling itself still decays physically, not via a token. Settling is skipped below 1% collapsed or at 100% collapsed.

keyboard: Tab moves through each action item in order.
Enter or Space activates the focused item.
semantics: The bar exposes a bottom toolbar landmark; the embedded FAB keeps its own button semantics distinct from the action row.

notes.text: comp.bottom-app-bar.container-elevation resolves to level2, but the fixed bar's Compose default is a hardcoded 0dp — the elevated look comes entirely from container-color already being the tonal surface-container value, not from an applied tonal-elevation shadow.

The flexible bar passes the top app bar's container-elevation token (level0/0dp) as its tonalElevation, not comp.bottom-app-bar.container-elevation — a cross-component token reuse worth preserving rather than "fixing" to the bottom-app-bar token.

Both variants share one private layout function upstream; a from-scratch implementation can likewise treat fixed and flexible as one container with swappable height/padding/arrangement rather than two components.

Content padding (4dp) and FAB padding are deliberately shrunk to net out against each button's own hit-target expansion, not the visible target — the visual result still meets the platform's minimum touch target.
